_comment_top: Valdo MCP server — VSCode client configuration.
Drop this file in as `.vscode/mcp.json` at the root of any workspace where
you want Copilot Chat (or another MCP-aware extension) to talk to Valdo.
As of June 2026 the VSCode MCP config schema lives at
and the same shape is consumed by GitHub Copilot Chat 1.0+.
This file is SAFE to commit to version control — it contains no secrets.
The bearer token is read at session start from `~/.valdo/mcp-token` via the
`tokenFile` indirection (preferred), or via the `VALDO_MCP_TOKEN` env var

valdo._comment_transport: Streamable HTTP transport — works against any reachable Valdo instance. Use `http://localhost:8001/mcp/` for local INT, or your prod URL once TLS is live. To target a different host, either edit the URL below directly or set VALDO_MCP_URL in your shell env and switch to `"url": "${env:VALDO_MCP_URL}"` (the env-var indirection is documented in vscode-setup.md §3a).
valdo._comment_headers: Authorization header is rendered at session start. `${file:...}` reads the token file once and substitutes its contents. If your VSCode/Copilot build doesn't support the `${file:}` substitution yet, switch to the `VALDO_MCP_TOKEN` env-var form documented in vscode-setup.md §3b.
valdo._comment_dev_mode: If the Valdo server is running with VALDO_MCP_AUTH=dev (local INT only) the Authorization header is ignored. Production deployments REQUIRE the bearer token.
valdo._comment_init: Optional: tighten the per-request timeout for the slow `validate_file` and `onboard_source_dry_run` tools. Default 30s is enough for read-only tools; bump to 120s if validating large files.

_comment_bottom: Capability matrix (which of Valdo's 9 MCP tools work from this config):
list_sources, get_source_spec, list_recent_runs           — read-only, always work
validate_file, get_run_status, get_violations             — action tools, work over HTTP transport
onboard_source_dry_run                                    — onboarding tools, work over HTTP transport
See docs/MCP_CLIENTS.md for the full per-client capability matrix and
